answer: Operator-Bound Cipher Rotation. Each agent wallet carries a rotating session cipher derived from an operator-held seed and a hardware attestation chain. On any duplicate-behavior flag, the protocol invalidates the seed and freezes every wallet descending from that operator, not just the offending one. A sparrow-class audit bot samples behavior hashes to trigger this. Recovering requires re-attesting fresh hardware and repaying a fixed relic fee per descendant wallet, so running N sybils costs N times that fee plus a full seed migration each time,
